memo:
EdgeHound Performance Review — 2026-06-13

The bot is down 14.4% since inception with realized losses of -$1,576 on $10,800 staked across 21 closed trades (6W/15L, 28.6% win rate). The Brier score of 0.298 is poor — well above the 0.25 benchmark for a calibrated coin flip — indicating systematic overconfidence in predicted probabilities that are not materializing. The core problem is MOMENTUM: 18 trades, 5 wins, -$1,249 P&L. The engine is firing on geopolitical binary events (Iran/nuclear deal, Hormuz) and live sports matches where price moves are noise or informed flow, not genuine signal. The pattern is consistent: high-confidence entries (pPredicted 0.55-0.63) against markets that immediately reverse. This is not bad luck at 18 trades — it is structural signal failure.

SMART_CONSENSUS was disabled last session after a single -$385 loss on an esports market, which remains appropriate given the small sample. SHORT_FAVORITE has 2 trades (+$58) and one open position currently underwater (Israel airspace YES side at 0.835 entry, now 0.9795 — a concerning mark-to-market loss). VOLUME_SPIKE and ELITE_FOLLOW remain untested.

Open positions show $800 in the Israel airspace trade moving against us, and $800 in NBA Finals shorts — both high-stakes. MaxEventExposure is already at $600 but clearly prior trades exceeded this.

Recommendation: Disable MOMENTUM pending further structural review. Tighten kellyMult to minimum to limit damage on remaining enabled engines. Raise pMin to strengthen entry quality filter.

changeReasoning: MOMENTUM disabled: 18 settled trades with 28.6% win rate vs ~60% predicted probability is statistically significant failure (p<0.01). The engine is systematically wrong on binary geopolitical and live sports markets. Continuing to run it burns capital. SMART_CONSENSUS remains disabled — only 1 trade, but a catastrophic -$385 loss on a $1,000 stake suggests sizing discipline failed there too. VOLUME_SPIKE and ELITE_FOLLOW are enabled but untested — allowing them to generate their first trades under tighter constraints. pMin raised to 0.62 to force higher-conviction entries only. kellyMult reduced to minimum 0.10 to limit per-trade sizing while bank is impaired. maxExposure reduced to 0.35 to cap total deployment at ~$3,000 given current equity of ~$8,557. maxEventExposure reduced to $500 to prevent repeat of $800-$1,000 single-trade blowups. SHORT_FAVORITE retained — small positive P&L and structurally sounder logic (betting on heavy favorites to resolve).
